transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Priya (Atlas Platform), Evan (Atlas SRE), Nadia (Atlas Security), Tom (Atlas Product)

Summary: quick weekly check-in for POC onboarding gating. Main threads: credentials contingency (one-time VPN vs VPC peering), latency triage for 95th percentile, quantization/kv cache tuning, and security artifact exchange. Agreed next steps and owners at end.

Topics: credentials handoff; dedicated vs hosted fallback; latency profiles and benchmark gaps; security docs (SOC2, ISO, KMS); rollout gating and canary timing.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll run through the agenda quickly. main goals today are to close the credential gap and get a clear path for the 95th pct latency test.
00:18 Priya: hey, quick note, we blocked a peering window on tuesday but we still need the service account creds. we tried the gateway token yesterday and it failed with a 403, not sure if our firewall blocked the CB.
00:35 Maya: ok, sounds like maybe the gateway key wasnt propagated. i'll resend the onboarding doc and also attach the token exchange steps. sometimes the token TTL is short and folks get 403s. also note that prefix caching (K-V cash) needs a specific header - i've seen it dropped by some proxies.
00:52 Evan: on the latency side, our initial 95th pct numbers looked fine at low qps but when we push to 400-600 concurrent users the p95 jumps a lot, like 700-900ms which is a blocker.
01:10 Jordan: that matches what we saw in early bench runs; could be batching misconfig or an autoscaler ramp. are you running through our hosted endpoint or the dedicated trial pool?
01:25 Priya: still hosted; we havent enabled the dedicated pool because of procurement. procurement wants to see the p95 for hosted first, then we discuss dedicated pricing.
01:40 Maya: two quick things — first, try a smaller batch size and enable continuous batching with the redis-backed queue, that often lowers tail latency. second, check your average sequence length; if you have lots of long prompts the kernel selection can flip to less optimal paths and latencies spike.
01:58 Tom: when you say kernel selection, is that the redwood runtime picking different kernels based on seq len? how deterministic is that?
02:15 Maya: yes, it's heuristics based — the runtime will pick a different path for >1024 tokens vs <512. sometimes quantized kernels also change perf. so that interplay can cause non-linear effects.
02:33 Nadia: security question — for the dedicated pool option we need KMS/HSM integration details and proof of zero access to plaintext keys. also we need an audit log example showing token-level access events.
02:50 Jordan: we can share the KMS integration guide and an example audit log export. i'll put those links in the recap. quick caveat: for on-prem / air-gapped installs we have a different packaging model and a longer lead time.
03:08 Evan: another issue: we saw 5xx spikes during a particular test when KV cache warmed; it seems the cache eviction caused a backend fallthrough and hit larger model variants. there was a couple second stall.
03:28 Maya: yep, cache warm/hot miss can cause fallback. recommended mitigation: pre-warm common prefixes and set a sticky routing policy to avoid cross-model fallbacks in the middle of a spike. also consider smaller model shards for latency-sensitive endpoints.
03:48 Priya: procurement flagged data residency, we need to know where logs and traces stay and for how long — is there a retention config?
04:05 Jordan: on hosted, logs are stored in our EU or US region depending on your tenancy; retention is configurable via the console. for Dedicated we can negotiate retention windows in the SOW. for Private installs, everything stays in your VPC by default.
04:25 Nadia: SSO is important — we use Okta with SAML. will Redwood support IdP-initiated SAML plus SCIM provisioning and RBAC groups?
04:40 Maya: yes, we support SAML SSO, SCIM, and RBAC mapping. there are a couple caveats around delegated admin for canary rollouts; we'll send the mapping table.
04:58 Tom: another product question — what are success criteria for the POC from your perspective? we want to make sure both sides agree.
05:12 Jordan: good callout. our typical success criteria are: 1) p95 latency under target (you said 900ms initial target), 2) stability for 48h at target load, 3) no security blockers (SOC2 artifacts + SSO provisioning), and 4) a pilot SOW signed for dedicated pool if performance is verified.
05:33 Priya: our internal bar is p95 <750ms for interactive flows, and batch embeddings under 150ms per request at our scale.
05:48 Maya: noted — we can optimize for interactive flows first. i'll produce a quantization profile and batch sizing recommendation tuned for 750ms p95 on hosted; if that doesnt meet target, we move to a small dedicated pool canary.
06:05 Evan: can we define the exact scenarios? i'm thinking 3 profiles: interactive chat (avg seq 350 tokens), long generation (avg 1500 tokens), and embeddings batch (avg 512). we'll run those in the spreadsheet you sent but i need the template.
06:25 Jordan: i'll re-share the benchmark template link. please populate the input distributions and attach perf logs. if possible, enable request tracing for the run so we can isolate kernel switchovers and KV cache misses.
06:45 Priya: on credentials contingency — if peering is delayed we asked about a temporary VPN + bastion approach. is that supported?
07:02 Maya: supported but not ideal; VPN means more network hops and typically higher latency. we can sign off a temporary VPN approach for onboarding, but we should treat it as a contingency and not the long-term plan.
07:18 Nadia: does the VPN option change our security posture? we need to ensure the tunnels are MFA and restrict egress.
07:30 Jordan: yes, we'll provide the minimal port list and recommended firewall rules. also we'll include the HSM/KMS flow for key provisioning over the tunnel.
07:47 Tom: curious about cost tradeoffs — you said dedicated pool has predictable throughput but costs more; is there a recommended staggered approach?
08:05 Maya: common approach: start hosted for discovery, optimize batching and quant profiles; if p95 can't be met, add a small reserved pool for the most latency-sensitive endpoints and route via smart routing policies. that limits cost while improving SLOs.
08:28 Evan: routing policies — can we pin a route to a specific model variant so that it never falls back?
08:40 Maya: yes, you can pin by model version and tier. we also have automatic fallback rules if capacity is exhausted; those are configurable per-route.
08:55 Priya: one last ops question — can you expose token-level billing details in the console for our cost tracking? we need per-route token counts.
09:08 Jordan: yes, token-level cost and latency breakdowns are available; we'll give you a sample dashboard and CSV export for ingestion into your cost analytics.
09:25 Maya: quick note on quant profiles — for your embedding flows we recommend 4-bit quant on model X-2 and fp16 on long-generation flows; i'll include the tradeoff table.
09:42 Nadia: security followup — please include encryption-at-rest details, where keys live (customer-managed KMS?), and how audit logs are delivered (S3 vs push).
10:00 Jordan: we'll include both options in the doc packet.
10:15 Tom: ok i think we're aligned on the plan.

Recap (final 5 minutes):
10:30 Jordan: action owners — Maya to send quant guide and batch spreadsheet, me to send SOC2 + network runbook and benchmark template, Priya to validate peering creds or confirm VPN contingency by 2026-06-20, Nadia to review security artifacts by 2026-06-23, and Atlas to run defined scenarios and share perf logs by 2026-06-24. schedule follow-up canary for 2026-06-29.
10:55 Priya: confirmed. thanks everyone.
11:00 Jordan: thanks, talk soon.

References shared: benchmark-template.csv (link), SOC2-summary.pdf (link), network-runbook.md (link), quant-profile-recommendation.pdf (link)

Note: transcript has a few mis-transcribed items (e.g. K-V cash = KV cache, some speaker labels merged).
